top_signals.title: IMF Warns Middle East War Could Derail Global Economic Growth
top_signals.summary: The energy crisis sparked by the war in the Middle East remains the biggest risk for the global economy, but investment in artificial intelligence provides grounds for optimism, the International Monetary Fund has said, expecting global growth of 3.4% next year. “The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits, so we need to move from just coping to rebuilding,” the institution’s chief economist, Silvana Tenreyro, told the media, as quoted by Reuters. “We need to restore fiscal space. top_signals.title: Mixed outlook for energy expenditures this winter
top_signals.summary: We expect energy expenditures this winter to vary because of diverging trends in energy prices among fuels and regional variation in forecast temperatures. We expect that lower prices for natural gas and propane will drive decreases in expenditures this year for the half of U.S. households heating with those fuels. Higher prices for electricity and heating oil drive increased expenditures for households heating with those fuels in our forecast.
